name: Stavros Niarchos Foundation Library (SNFL)
why_included: Former Mid-Manhattan; ~44k sq ft public space with double the seats; free rooftop terrace (first-come); open to 8pm weekdays.

name: Stephen A. Schwarzman Building - Rose Main Reading Room
why_included: Rose Main Reading Room open for quiet study without appointment; free wifi and outlets at long tables. Silent, solo work only.

name: Jefferson Market Library
why_included: Landmark courthouse renovated 2022; second-floor Adult Reading Room for study; open to 8pm Mon-Thu.

name: 53rd Street Library
why_included: Modern TEN Arquitectos branch near MoMA with oak bleacher amphitheater and a laptop bar.

name: New York Public Library for the Performing Arts
why_included: Quiet research library at Lincoln Center; personal laptops allowed in reading rooms; pair with the Rubenstein Atrium next door.

name: Bloomingdale Library
why_included: UWS branch with a bookable 2nd-floor Study Room (reserve a timeslot); useful for small-group sessions, verify capacity.

name: Inwood Library
why_included: Brand-new library opened June 2024 in The Eliza building; bright, modern northern Manhattan option.

name: Battery Park City Library
why_included: Big windows over Teardrop Park; reviews cite ample seating with power outlets; can get noisy with kids.

name: Mulberry Street Library
why_included: Converted chocolate factory; underground adult reading rooms with work tables, plenty of outlets and comfortable seating (NYU News 2023).

name: Fort Washington Library
why_included: 111-year-old Carnegie branch reopened January 2025 after a five-year closure; renovated and accessible.

name: Washington Heights Library
why_included: Multi-floor renovated branch with new teen area and tech center; uptown study option.

name: Muhlenberg Library
why_included: Reopened after extensive renovation with new furnishings and tech; free wifi; open to 7pm Mon-Thu.

name: Hudson Park Library
why_included: Historic Carnegie branch reopened January 2024 after basement repairs; quiet West Village option.

name: 125th Street Library
why_included: Landmarked branch reopened Oct 2024 after $34M renovation; new teen center, elevator, upgraded heating and cooling.

name: Brooklyn Public Library - Central Library
why_included: Info Commons public co-working space (room and outlets for 70+ laptops); bookable meeting rooms; open 9am-8pm Mon-Thu. Group.

name: Brooklyn Heights Library
why_included: Opened 2022; co-working seating throughout, reservable mezzanine conference rooms, laptop loans; open Sundays. Group.

name: Greenpoint Library and Environmental Education Center
why_included: LEED-Gold building; lounge seating, small meeting rooms, laptop loans; rooftop garden sometimes open for quiet study; open Sundays. Group.

name: Sunset Park Library
why_included: New 20,000+ sq ft branch opened Nov 2023; reservable meeting rooms and recording studio; open to 8pm Tue/Thu. Group.

name: Williamsburgh Library
why_included: Historic branch with reservable meeting rooms; fully accessible; open to 8pm Tue/Thu. Group via room booking.

name: Pacific Library
why_included: Near Barclays Center; reservable meeting rooms; open to 8pm Tue/Thu. Group via room booking.

name: Park Slope Library
why_included: Neighborhood branch with reservable meeting rooms; fully accessible; open to 8pm Tue/Thu. Group via room booking.

name: Bedford Library
why_included: Brooklyn's oldest branch reopened April 2025 after four-year renovation with new heating and cooling.

name: Hunters Point Library
why_included: Steven Holl-designed waterfront library with skyline views; free wifi; open seven days incl. Sundays.

name: Broadway Library (QPL)
why_included: Renovated 2024: computer center with tables for laptop use and multiple charging outlets; classroom/meeting space.

name: Long Island City Library (QPL)
why_included: Free wifi and computer workstations; open to 8pm Thursdays; wifi reachable outside even when closed.

name: Steinway Library (QPL)
why_included: Free wifi and computer workstations; open to 8pm Thursdays; nearest alternative while Astoria branch is closed.

name: 590 Madison Avenue Atrium (former IBM atrium)
why_included: Glass bamboo atrium; required 32 movable tables and 110 chairs; free wifi and cafe per Untapped; 8am-10pm. Group.

name: 550 Madison Avenue Garden
why_included: Snohetta-redesigned covered garden (not fully enclosed); seating and benches throughout; open daily 7am-11pm year-round.

name: Park Avenue Plaza atrium
why_included: Enclosed 30-ft atrium; required 48 tables and 136 movable seats; Untapped notes tables for studying/working; 8am-10pm. Group.

name: 875 Third Avenue atrium
why_included: Three-level atrium; required ~67 tables and 250 chairs; 2025 visitor photos show second-level tables; open to 11pm Mon-Sat. Group.

name: Citigroup Center atrium (The Hugh)
why_included: Covered atrium required to have ~50 movable tables and 170+ seats; The Hugh food hall inside; 7am-11pm. Group.

name: 180 Maiden Lane atrium
why_included: APOPS calls it downtown's best indoor POPS; 24 tables, 120 chairs, restrooms, kiosk; visitors report wifi, limited outlets. Group.

name: David Rubenstein Atrium at Lincoln Center
why_included: 38 movable tables, 152 chairs; free wifi per Lonely Planet; open daily (8am-10pm weekdays); cafe; busy during Thursday shows. Group.

name: Olympic Tower atrium
why_included: Covered arcade required to keep 26 tables, 78 chairs and a coffee bar; 8am-10pm; current conditions thinly documented.

name: Crystal Pavilion atrium
why_included: Concourse atrium with 18 movable tables, 60 chairs and restrooms; weekdays 8am-7pm only; status unverified since 2023.

name: Winter Garden at Brookfield Place
why_included: Palm-filled glass atrium; free wifi per AAA; Workfrom notes group seating, tables, limited outlets; food halls adjacent. Group.

name: Urban Garden Room at One Bryant Park
why_included: Indoor POPS off the lobby with seating areas and coffee shop; Chashama lists 72-person capacity; chess players welcome.

name: Oculus (World Trade Center)
why_included: Free WTC wifi throughout and some seating areas; few tables, so better for short sessions than long workdays.
